title: The Year Dunzo's Paydays Kept Moving
dek: In 2023 Dunzo, an early leader in Indian quick commerce, delayed salaries again and again while its chief executive looked for money; by 2025 it was in insolvency proceedings.

story.event: Repeatedly deferring staff salaries while seeking funds after the quick-commerce expansion, ahead of insolvency
story.summary: After raising $240 million led by Reliance Retail in January 2022 to expand its 15-to-20-minute Dunzo Daily grocery service, Bengaluru's Dunzo ran short of cash in 2023, laid off staff, closed dark stores and repeatedly deferred salaries while chief executive Kabeer Biswas sought new funding. Co-founders left, the workforce fell to about 50 in September 2024, Biswas joined Flipkart in January 2025, and on 6 August 2025 the National Company Law Tribunal admitted Dunzo into insolvency proceedings.
paragraphs: On Friday 15 September 2023, at an internal meeting in Bengaluru, Kabeer Biswas, Dunzo's co-founder and chief executive, told staff that the June and July pay already held back from them would now arrive in November. By reports at the time, he warned that more layoffs could follow if cash ran shorter, said the company would try to give up its office to cut costs, and promised September's salaries on time. It was the fourth time the date had moved.

Twenty months earlier Dunzo had looked like a leader. It began as an app that would fetch and deliver almost anything across a city, and in 2017 became Google's first direct investment in an Indian start-up. In 2021 it launched Dunzo Daily, delivering groceries within about 20 minutes from neighbourhood warehouses called dark stores. In January 2022 it raised $240 million, $200 million from Reliance Retail for a 25.8 per cent stake. Biswas told the Economic Times he would grow from about 60 dark stores to 200 within six to nine months, and said Dunzo aimed to become "one of the most reliable quick commerce providers in the country". Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy's Instamart were chasing the same customers.

In the year to March 2023 Dunzo lost about ₹1,800 crore on revenue of about ₹227 crore. That April it raised $75 million from investors including Reliance and Google and laid off about 30 per cent of its staff; it also closed about half its dark stores and moved to a mix of its own stores and partner shops. From June, pay was capped and then deferred, with 12 per cent annual interest promised on what was held back. Biswas, one source told the Economic Times, was wholly focused on fundraising. In October co-founder Dalvir Suri left.

In December the company told staff that investor money was on its way and asked them to plan for a worst case of 15 December. Vendors took unpaid bills to the National Company Law Tribunal. In September 2024 Dunzo cut its workforce by three-quarters, to about 50 people. In January 2025 Biswas, the last co-founder still there, joined Flipkart to run its quick-commerce service. Reliance wrote off its investment, and on 6 August 2025 the tribunal admitted Dunzo into insolvency proceedings.

quote.text: The people are as the root and the king as the tree; and the tree, O son, gains strength from the root.
quote.locator: Chapter I, "Concerning Justice, Counsel, and the Administration of Government", Nushiravan's counsel to his son
quote.source_title: The Bustān of Sadi, tr. A. Hart Edwards, Project Gutenberg eBook #60471
quote.connection: Saadi has a dying king tell his son that the tree draws its strength from its roots. Biswas spent Dunzo's last stretch chasing the money that might have paid his people, while, by one account, others did most of the talking with them. Whether that was tending the root or leaving it, the line does not say.

reflection: Each moved date at Dunzo was a date someone had planned their rent around. When money is late, the pull is to name the next date with confidence and hope it holds. The harder kindness is to say plainly what is known and what is not, as the December message did when it asked people to plan for the worst case.

You may one day wait on money that others depend on, or wait yourself on someone else's promise. Either way, it helps to separate the date you hope for from the date you can stand behind, and to say out loud which one you are giving.
invitation: Look at one promise you have made with a date attached. Ask whether it is the date you hope for or the date you can stand behind, and if it is the first, tell the person today.

sources.title: Dunzo raises US$240M in a round led by Reliance Retail (media release, 6 January 2022, filed with the stock exchanges)
sources.publisher: Reliance Industries Limited / Reliance Retail Ventures (NSE archive)
sources.supports: $240 million round led by Reliance Retail, which invested $200 million for 25.8% on a fully diluted basis; Dunzo Daily launched in Bengaluru, delivering essentials in 15-20 minutes from micro-warehouses; expansion from 7 to 15 cities; Biswas's statement including 'one of the most reliable quick commerce providers in the country'; founders Kabeer Biswas, Mukund Jha, Dalvir Suri and Ankur Aggarwal

sources.title: Reliance enters quick commerce by picking up 26 percent stake in Dunzo (January 2022)
sources.supports: Dunzo started as a hyperlocal pick-up and drop app; Google's first direct investment in an Indian startup in 2017; Dunzo Daily launched in Bengaluru in August 2021; Biswas told the Economic Times dark stores would grow from 60 to 200 in six to nine months; competitors Blinkit, Instamart and Zepto

sources.title: Reliance Retail invests $200 mn in Dunzo; to pick 25.8% stake (6 January 2022)
sources.supports: $240 million round and Reliance Retail's $200 million for 25.8%; Dunzo Daily delivering in 15-20 minutes; Zepto and Blinkit as rivals

sources.title: India's Reliance-backed Dunzo defers pending salary dues till Sept - memo (July 2023, Reuters)
sources.supports: Pending salaries since June deferred to September; 50% of dark stores reduced, layoffs and salary delays; salaries capped at 75,000 rupees a month; $75 million raised in April from investors including Reliance Retail and Alphabet alongside about 30% layoffs

sources.title: Dunzo Delays Salaries Yet Again; CEO Warns Of Another Round Of Layoffs (September 2023)
sources.supports: Biswas told employees at an internal meeting on Friday 15 September (per the Economic Times) that June and July pay would come in November; warning of further layoffs; promise to pay September salaries on time; plan to vacate the Wind Tunnel Road office; the fourth major delay; earlier layoff of 30% (300 people); shutting most dark stores and moving to a marketplace model

sources.title: Dunzo now defers employee salaries to November, may vacate office space (September 2023, IANS)
sources.supports: Biswas's town hall announcing the delay to November and a possible move out of the office; hybrid model of dark stores and partner stores; 12% annual interest promised on the salary held back from June; about $500 million raised to date

sources.title: Dunzo Cofounder Dalvir Suri To Exit Financially Stressed Startup (October 2023)
sources.supports: Biswas's email of 1 October announcing Suri's exit and his statement to Inc42; the Economic Times source's account that Suri and Mukund Jha handled most staff conversations while Biswas was fully focused on fundraising; a stalled $100 million Series G and efforts to raise $35-40 million

sources.title: Dunzo fails to pay salaries again (December 2023)
sources.supports: November salaries unpaid; the company's message that investor funds would be wired and its advice to plan for a worst-case timeline of 15 December 2023; FY23 loss of about ₹1,800 crore

sources.title: Why Dunzo is Battling Financial Insolvency and Vendor Dues (2024)
sources.supports: Vendor insolvency applications to the NCLT, including Betterplace Safety Solutions over about ₹4 crore; FY23 loss of ₹1,801.8 crore on operating revenue of ₹226.6 crore; Deloitte's going-concern doubt; board exits by Reliance Retail and Google representatives in 2023

sources.title: Kabeer Biswas Leaves Dunzo, Joins Flipkart's Growing Quick Commerce Segment 'Minutes' (13 January 2025)
sources.supports: Biswas, the sole remaining co-founder, joining Flipkart to head its quick-commerce service Minutes; Dunzo's layoff of 75% of its employees in September 2024, leaving about 50

sources.title: Reliance-Backed Dunzo Admitted Into Insolvency (2025)
sources.supports: NCLT Bengaluru admission of Dunzo into the corporate insolvency resolution process on vendors' petitions; Reliance's write-off of its $240 million investment; about $485 million raised in total; Suri, Jha and Biswas's departures

sources.title: Insolvency Proceedings Against Dunzo Digital Take New Turn (2025)
sources.supports: The NCLT's record that Dunzo had been admitted into insolvency on 6 August 2025 on a petition by Velvin Packaging Solutions, with an interim resolution professional appointed; Reliance's write-off

cross_checks.claim: In January 2022 Dunzo raised $240 million, with Reliance Retail investing $200 million for 25.8%.
In September 2023 Biswas told employees that deferred June and July salaries would be paid in November.
In 2023 Dunzo raised $75 million, laid off about 30% of staff and cut about half its dark stores.
Dunzo lost about ₹1,800 crore in the year to March 2023.
Biswas left in January 2025 to join Flipkart's quick-commerce business.
Dunzo was admitted into insolvency proceedings by the NCLT Bengaluru bench in August 2025, after Reliance wrote off its investment.

research_notes: FY23 figures disagree: Outlook Business, Inc42's article body and MediaNama give a loss of ₹1,801.8 crore (Entrepreneur rounds to ₹1,800 crore); Inc42's summary gives ₹1,748 crore against revenue of ₹206.5 crore (probably a different basis); revenue is ₹226.6 crore in Outlook and Inc42's body but ₹266 crore in MediaNama (likely a typo). The story uses about ₹1,800 crore and about ₹227 crore. Total raised: about $485 million (Inc42, Legal Era) or about $500 million (The News Minute); not used in the story. Founding year: 2014 (MediaNama 2022, Entrepreneur, Inc42's Suri article, Legal Era) vs 2015 (Republic World, MediaNama 2025, Inc42's admission story); the story gives no year. Layoffs: Reuters and Inc42 give about 30% (about 300 people) in April 2023, while Outlook Business says more than 1,300 employees were laid off in 2023; the story uses the dated 30% figure. Co-founder exits: Inc42 dates Suri's exit to October 2023 and Jha's later; Outlook puts both in 2023; the story mentions only Suri. The first insolvency plea by Velvin Packaging is dated November 2023 by Outlook and September 2024 by Inc42; the story does not date the vendor petitions and gives only the tribunal's admission date of 6 August 2025 (Legal Era, citing the NCLT order). Reliance's write-off is reported as $240 million (its total investment across rounds); the story says only that it wrote off its investment. The account that Biswas was focused on fundraising while co-founders handled staff conversations is from an unnamed source quoted by the Economic Times via Inc42 and is attributed as such. Causes of the collapse are not assigned beyond the documented sequence; no court or regulator finding of fault is reported. Biswas reportedly drew no salary for about 20 months (YourStory, January 2025), but that page is blocked for the verifier, so the detail is not used. The Saadi passage is a dying king's advice on ruling; it is applied by analogy to a company and its staff.
